key_insight: DiffSimuQ transforms analog quantum experiments into executable derivative experiments whose expected outcomes exactly equal the desired gradients.
engineering_relevance: Source and derivative experiments share a compiler that lowers branches to neutral-atom controls and selects gradient strategies by estimated cost.
method: Compositionally transform experiment programs without accessing the internal quantum state.
Use the Nyquist shift rule for general time-dependent evolution, including non-commuting controls.
Use sampled-time parameter-shift insertions for involutory generators.
evidence_signal: In machine-level noisy emulation, both methods avoid the finite-difference error floor and improve closed-loop optimization; at 1,000 qubits, each derivative branch adds at most 0.3% to source compilation time.
watch_item: Exact gradient identities do not eliminate sampling costs or hardware realization errors, and the reported evaluation uses emulation rather than physical-device experiments.
paper_title: Analog Quantum Experiments Meet Automatic Differentiation - from Programs to Atoms
